authoredSolutions.32: For a gas dissolved in a liquid, Henry's law gives \(p = K_{H}x\), where \(p\) is the partial pressure of the gas above the solution and \(x\) its mole fraction in solution. For \(CO_{2}\) in water at \(25^{\circ}C\), \(K_{H} \approx 1.67 \times 10^{3}\) bar, so \(\log K_{H}\) is positive and the line must cut the y-axis above the origin. The plot with a positive slope and a positive non-zero intercept is option (C); the line through the origin would require \(K_{H} = 1\), a negative slope contradicts direct proportionality, and a horizontal line would make \(p\) independent of \(x\).
